name: Kawaii Interactive Tracing Workbook for Kids (Sunflower Studio)
note: Content built and verified 2026-08-20: 71-page evergreen PDF. Real differentiator vs the saturated kawaii-worksheet category (per the market research that greenlit this line): genuine dashed-outline tracing extracted from actual Poppins Bold font glyph paths via a new tools/glyph_trace.py (fontTools -> reportlab Path -> dashed stroke), not a gray-fill approximation or a static coloring page. Contents: welcome, dashboard, index, a For Parents & Teachers tips page, 26 letter-tracing pages (upper + lowercase, each with real ruled 'now write it yourself' practice space, not just a trace-and-nothing-else claim), 20 number-tracing pages (trace + write-yourself + count-and-color), 8 shape-tracing pages, 5 sight-word pages (real Dolch pre-primer words, not invented), 4 math+coloring pages (real, correct addition facts), a 48-star reward chart cross-promoting the shop's existing sticker packs (this product does not need its own -- confirmed against the original spec), 2 blank practice pages. Two real completeness bugs found and fixed during verification: the letter and number pages originally said 'trace, then try on your own' but provided zero blank space for the 'own' part -- added real ruled practice lines. Also fixed a real glyph-positioning bug in glyph_trace.py itself (translate composing onto an already-scaled Group instead of a fresh wrapper, which nearly stacked every letter of a word on top of each other) before any content was built on top of it. validate_digital_file() clean, 7.0MB. STILL NOT BUILT: listing photos, listing title/tags/description. Status stays 'draft' until those close and Scott reviews. UPDATE 2026-08-20 (Scott caught on real device review): fixed a real overlap bug -- the bonus word-trace text was rendering on top of its own label (box too short, insufficient vertical gap). Also added a real per-page activity to every page type to use the large blank space Scott flagged, not just decorative filler: letter pages get a 'Letter Hunt' circle-the-letter grid (seeded per letter, reproducible), number pages get a 'trace the number word' bonus + a real before/after number-sequence exercise, shape pages get 3 blank 'draw your own' boxes + a real-world example tip, math pages expanded from 4 to 6 correct problems per page. Re-verified clean, 7.1MB. UPDATE 2026-08-20: added persistent navigation (Scott asked for a floating/sticky nav button while scrolling). True scroll-relative floating overlays don't exist in the PDF format -- pages are static, there's no CSS-position:fixed equivalent -- so built the honest working substitute instead: a 7-tab strip (HOME/Aa/123/SHP/WRD/1+1/FUN) in the same left-margin spot on every page, each tab a REAL clickable internal PDF link jumping straight to that section from anywhere in the document, current section dimmed. First real attempt used PyPDF2's merge_page() to stamp an overlay onto every page -- confirmed live this badly duplicates resources on pages that already carry many glyph Form XObjects (every tracing page does), ballooning the PDF from 7MB to 20MB, right at Etsy's hard limit. Fixed by drawing the tabs directly into each page's own canvas instead (shares existing font resources, zero size cost) and adding only the link annotations as a lightweight post-process. Also caught and fixed a second real bug before shipping: the original star/diamond tab icons aren't in Poppins-Bold's glyph set and rendered as blank colored boxes with no visible label -- switched to safe ASCII labels and added a build-time assertion that checks every nav label's characters against the font's real glyph set, so this class of bug fails loudly at build time instead of shipping silently. Re-verified all 71 pages render clean and every link resolves to the correct target page. 7.2MB. UPDATE 2026-08-20: fixed a real layout bug Scott caught on a real device -- the welcome/dashboard/index/parents pages' text and buttons started at the plain _ML margin (36pt), which sits inside the nav tab strip's zone (x=8-42), so headings and buttons were rendering with their left edge cut off under the tabs. All 4 pages (plus reward chart/practice, which used a narrower _ML+20) now use a shared CML constant (_ML+26) matching the offset the tracing pages already used correctly, and centered elements now center within the real content area instead of the full page width. Re-verified clean on every page type. UPDATE 2026-08-20: fixed a real ascender/descender overlap bug Scott caught on a real device (letter F's practice-line box touching the lowercase f's ascender). Root cause: the vertical gaps around each trace row assumed a typical short letter (like 'a'), but tall-ascender letters (b,d,f,h,k,l,t at 88pt) need ~66pt of headroom above baseline, well more than the 46pt gap provided -- the tall stroke visibly poked up into the ruled practice box above it. Fixed by widening the gaps around both trace rows to real worst-case clearance (not just what happens to fit 'a'). Verified against the actual worst cases across the whole document, not just the original bug report: letter pages with ascenders (F, K), descenders (G, P), and both at once (J, whose lowercase j has an ascender dot AND a descender tail) all clean; sight-word pages with ascender/descender words (find, funny, help) clean; number page 20 (longest word 'twenty', full 20-circle counting grid) clean; shape and math pages re-verified clean. Full 71-page render + validate_digital_file() pass. 7.2MB. UPDATE 2026-08-20: fixed a real print-visibility bug Scott caught on an actual printout -- 'the tracing letters do not show up very well, they need to be darker outlined.' Two distinct causes, fixed in order: (1) _trace_ink() previously blended the trace color only 55% toward the theme's dark ink, which still washed out badly on paper against the Sunflower Studio theme's inherently light-value yellow -- changed to use the dark ink color directly with zero blend, matching how real commercial tracing workbooks draw guides. (2) A separate, deeper bug in glyph_trace.py's dashed_glyph_group(): reportlab Path.strokeWidth/strokeDashArray are geometric properties in the glyph's OWN pre-transform coordinate space, and Group.scale() (applied to fit the glyph to size_pt) shrinks them right along with the outline -- invisible on the 88pt letter traces (stroke thinned to ~0.26pt) but the SAME code at size_pt=22 (the small 'trace the word' bonus boxes on both letter and number pages) shrank a requested stroke_w=2.0 to under 0.05pt, genuinely invisible on paper. Fixed by dividing both strokeWidth and strokeDashArray by the glyph's scale factor so the caller's requested absolute value is what actually lands on the page regardless of glyph size -- took three attempts to get right: compensating both first produced an oversized/blobby dash pattern at 22pt; compensating only strokeWidth (leaving dash natural) fixed 22pt but made the 88pt letters look dense and beady since the fixed-width stroke was now wider than the naturally-shrunk dash gaps; the final fix compensates both together, since dash length has to stay a real multiple of the actual (compensated) stroke width to read as a clean dashed line at any size, not a value relative to the glyph's own path length. Verified via direct pixel-crop renders at both sizes: 88pt letter traces (F/f) and 22pt word-trace boxes (Fish, and the identical-pattern number-word boxes) all now dark, clean, and legible; also spot-checked 34pt sight-word traces (unaffected by the bug in practice but re-confirmed clean regardless). Full 71-page clean-render + validate_digital_file() pass, zero errors, 7,168,824 bytes (7.17MB).
